text:
anya: Heads-up — console p95 for /v1/generate (cohort=mobile-short) spiked right after the routing policy tweak. p50 is flat but p95 jumped ~120ms. anyone else seeing this? :thinking:

sam: yup saw the alert. p99 moved a bit too. my hunch: fanout to embeddings or reranker is leaking into the endpoint rollup. question: do we tag fanout_target in rollups today?

anya: not in the rollups. raw tracing has `fanout_target` but our percentile rollup merge drops that dimension. so attribution is lost at the UI layer.

michael: that explains it — when heavy tails live in the downstream call we fold them into the parent endpoint percentile. the merge path currently sums samples without preserving fanout buckets.

sam: short-term mitigation idea: expose a "split by downstream" option on the latency panel so you can break p95 by `fanout_target` for the route. default off to avoid extra queries.

anya: useful. quick debug query I ran in traces: ```SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 95) AS p95, count() FROM traces WHERE route='/v1/generate' GROUP BY fanout_target, deployment ORDER BY p95 DESC LIMIT 10;``` that showed `embed-service` had a 300ms p95 while others were ~40ms.

jeremy: UX ask: when we enable split-by-downstream, surface sample_count and a small badge if sample_count < 100 (so folks don't overreact to tiny buckets). also a tiny inline explanation: "merged rollups may hide downstream tail latencies."

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry-flag enable-fanout-tags=true rolled to canary (3%) for eng-prod at 2024-11-09T12:15Z :rocket:

michael: after the canary flip, p95 on the main rollup decreased ~90ms for that cohort. looks like tagging worked and UI split showed the culprit. we still need to decide re-ingest vs. retroactive recalculation.

sam: follow-up actions: create ticket to (1) add split-by-downstream toggle + sample_count badge, (2) plan backfill/recalc for 48h window, (3) add an alert rule that fires on downstream-delta > 100ms. I'll open it now.

anya: thanks — pls @sam add the dashboard annotation for the routing policy change so it's obvious in history. i'll keep monitoring and post a short postmortem if the backfill shows larger impact. :thumbsup:
